title: Represent the full class-specific energy by polynomial shifts without claiming coercivity
statement: On H_c={h:sum_x c^x/x! |h(x)|^2<infinity}, let S_i h(x)=h(x+e_i),P_r(T)=T^z_r-T^y_r and extend f on Gamma by zero. Weak reversibility makes rho+y_r and rho+z_r lie in the same population component, so E(f,f)=(2Z)^-1 sum_r alpha_r||P_r(S)f_tilde||^2,alpha_r=kappa_r*c^y_r. The common closed form domain defines the closed row A=(sqrt(alpha_r/2)P_r(S))_r from the class-supported space into the ambient product. On an irreducible class ker A=span{1_Gamma}; the standard closed-range theorem gives positive Poincare gap iff Ran A is closed. Pinning one anchor gives the equivalent quotient with h(a)=0. This retains the infinite-domain coercivity obligation and does not provide a total decision algorithm or import an unverified bounded-differentiation theorem.
